facts.fact: Under UNCLOS the EEZ extends 200 nautical miles from the baseline.
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest point of the oceans (~10,935 m).
Samudrayaan will carry three persons to 6,000 m in the submersible MATSYA-6000.
The continental shelf is the gently sloping seaward extension of the continent (0–200 m), the richest fishing ground.
Mid-oceanic ridges form at divergent plate boundaries.
Ocean relief from the coast: shelf → slope → rise → abyssal plain → trench.
The Dead Sea is extremely saline because it is enclosed with high evaporation and no outlet.
The thermocline is the layer where temperature falls rapidly with depth.
The Gulf Stream is a warm current of the North Atlantic.
The Humboldt (Peru) current is a cold current of the south-east Pacific.
The Kuroshio is a warm current of the north-west Pacific.
The Benguela is a cold current of the south-east Atlantic.
Ocean water has physical (temperature, salinity, density), chemical (dissolved gases) and biological (plankton, nekton, benthos) characteristics.
Spring tides occur when the Sun, Earth and Moon are in a straight line (new and full moon).
Neap tides, the lowest range, occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles.
Tides are caused chiefly by the Moon's gravity, then the Sun's, with centrifugal force (UPSC 2015).
A tidal bore is a wall of water rushing up a river mouth on the rising tide (Hooghly).
Cold water rich in fresh river discharge is unfavourable for coral reefs.
Coral reef types are fringing, barrier and atoll.
Polymetallic nodules are chiefly manganese, nickel, copper and cobalt.
The December 2004 tsunami was caused by an undersea earthquake off Sumatra.
OTEC uses the temperature difference between warm surface and cold deep water.
Plastic and microplastic waste is a major marine pollutant, mitigated by cutting single-use plastics.
AP's coastline (~974 km) is the longest on India's east coast.
Visakhapatnam is AP's only major port.
AP is a leading state in fish and shrimp production.
Average ocean salinity is about 35 parts per thousand.
Salinity is highest in the subtropics and lower near the equator.
The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point of the Atlantic.
The Sunda (Java) Trench is the deepest point of the Indian Ocean.
The Tonga Trench is the second-deepest oceanic trench.
The Blue Economy is the sustainable use of ocean resources for growth, jobs and ecosystem health.
The Equatorial Counter Current flows east because the North and South Equatorial Currents converge and pile up water (UPSC 2015).
The January–March Ocean Mean Temperature is used to assess whether monsoon rainfall will be above or below the mean (UPSC 2020).
At Chandipur (Odisha) the sea recedes a few km twice a day.
More water is stored in polar ice caps and glaciers than as groundwater; groundwater exceeds rivers and lakes (UPSC 2021/2013).
The Deep Ocean Mission was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
MATSYA-6000 is built by NIOT, Chennai.
India's coral reefs: Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar (not the Sundarbans).
Coral bleaching is the loss of symbiotic zooxanthellae due to warming.
INCOIS, Hyderabad runs the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre.
India's EEZ is about 2.37 million km².
Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada and Machilipatnam are important non-major ports of AP.
India's tidal-energy potential lies in the Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Khambhat and Sundarbans.
Most coral reefs are in tropical waters; over one-third lie off Australia, Indonesia and the Philippines (UPSC 2018).
Oceanography is the study of all aspects of the oceans.
'Ocean' comes from the Greek 'Oceanus', an enormous river encircling the Earth.
The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.
The Pacific, the largest ocean, covers about one-third of the Earth's surface — more than all the land.
Ferdinand Magellan named the Pacific ("peaceful").
The Pacific's average depth is about 4,280 m.
The International Date Line lies in the Pacific.
The Atlantic, the second-largest ocean, covers about 20% of the Earth's surface and is S-shaped.
The Atlantic is named after Atlas (Atlantis Thalassa).
The Atlantic's average depth is about 3,646 m; the Puerto Rico Trench reaches about 8,376 m.
Greenland, the world's largest island, lies in the Atlantic.
The Sargasso Sea is the only sea without a shore.
The Indian Ocean is the warmest ocean and is land-locked on the north.
Madagascar is the largest island of the Indian Ocean.
The Sunda (Java) Trench is about 7,450 m deep.
The Southern Ocean lies around Antarctica south of 60°S.
The Drake Passage, between Cape Horn and the South Shetland Islands, links the Southern Ocean with the Atlantic and Pacific.
The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest ocean, with the lowest salinity.
The Molloy Deep in the Fram Strait is the Arctic Ocean's deepest point.
The Arctic joins the Pacific through the Bering Strait.
Pacific marginal seas include the Coral, South China, Tasman, Bering and Okhotsk seas.
Atlantic marginal seas include the Caribbean, Mediterranean, North and Baltic seas and Hudson Bay.
Weddell and Ross seas are marginal seas of the Southern Ocean.
The Pacific is linked to the Indian Ocean via the Indonesian seaways, Torres Strait and Strait of Malacca.
The Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.
The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
The Nine Degree Channel separates Lakshadweep (Kavaratti) from Minicoy.
The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
Duncan Passage lies between South Andaman and Little Andaman.
The Coco Channel lies between the Andaman Islands and Myanmar's Coco Islands.
The Strait of Malacca separates Malaysia and Sumatra, joining the Andaman Sea and South China Sea.
The Sunda Strait separates Java and Sumatra.
The Strait of Hormuz joins the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.
Bab-el-Mandeb joins the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain and Morocco, joining the Mediterranean and Atlantic.
The Bosphorus joins the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara.
The Dardanelles join the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea.
The Strait of Dover separates England and France.
The Bering Strait separates Asia (Russia) and North America (Alaska).
The Strait of Magellan separates mainland South America from Tierra del Fuego.
The Torres Strait separates Australia and New Guinea.
The Bass Strait separates Australia and Tasmania.
The Cook Strait separates the North and South Islands of New Zealand.
The Taiwan (Formosa) Strait separates China and Taiwan; the Korea Strait separates Korea and Japan.
La Perouse Strait separates Sakhalin and Hokkaido.
The Florida Strait separates Florida and Cuba.
The Davis Strait separates Greenland and Baffin Island.
The Strait of Messina separates Italy and Sicily; Otranto separates Italy and Albania.
The Mozambique Channel separates Mozambique and Madagascar.
The Suez Canal (1869) joins the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
The Panama Canal (1914) joins the Atlantic and the Pacific.
Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) lies in the Palk Strait region.
Horizontal ocean movements are currents and waves; vertical ones are tides and upwelling.
In waves the energy moves, not the water; particles move in small circles.
A wave breaks when the water depth is less than half its wavelength.
The largest waves are found in the open ocean.
Steep waves are young and local; slow, steady swells come from far away.
Wave height depends on wind strength, duration and fetch.
Wave amplitude is half the wave height.
Wave period is the time between two successive crests passing a fixed point.
Wavelength is the horizontal distance between two successive crests.
Wave speed is measured in knots.
Constructive waves have a stronger swash than backwash and build beaches.
Destructive waves have a stronger backwash, are high and steep, and erode the coast.
Surges are irregular sea-level rises caused by winds and pressure changes, unlike tides.
The Moon's tidal attraction is more than twice the Sun's.
Gravity and centrifugal force create two tidal bulges — towards and away from the Moon.
Tidal bulges are higher on wide continental shelves and lower at mid-ocean islands.
Semi-diurnal tides (two highs, two lows a day) are the most common.
Diurnal tides have one high and one low a day.
Mixed tides occur along the west coast of North America and many Pacific islands.
Neap tides come about seven days after spring tides.
At perigee, and at perihelion (3 January), tidal ranges are greater than normal.
The falling tide is the ebb; the rising tide is the flow or flood.
The Bay of Fundy (Canada) has the greatest tidal range.
Tides aid navigation over harbour bars, desilt estuaries and generate power (Canada, France, Russia, China).
Sihwa Lake (South Korea, 254 MW) is a major tidal power station; La Rance is in France.
Tidal power is generated by floodgate dams, tidal barrages and tidal stream generators.
The Gulf of Cambay (Khambhat) has a tidal range of up to 11 m and the Gulf of Kutch 8 m.
A tidal project at Durgaduani creek in the Sundarbans (3.75 MW, approved 2008) was delayed.
A 50 MW tidal plant is being developed at Mandavi (Kutch); a 250 MW plant was planned in the Gulf of Kutch.
India's coastline is usually given as over 7,500 km; a 2024 re-measurement gives about 11,098 km.
Surface currents occupy the upper 400 m and are driven mainly by wind.
Deep currents (thermohaline circulation) are driven by density differences of temperature and salinity.
Gyres turn clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and anticlockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
The North Atlantic Drift, a warm continuation of the Gulf Stream, keeps Western Europe mild.
The Labrador current is a cold current off Newfoundland.
The Canary current is a cold current off north-west Africa, adding to the Sahara's aridity.
The warm Brazil current meets the cold Falkland current off Argentina.
The Norwegian current is a warm extension of the North Atlantic Drift.
The California current is a cold current of the North Pacific.
The cold Oyashio flows south along Japan and meets the warm Kuroshio.
The East Australian current is warm.
The Kamchatka current is a cold extension of the Oyashio.
The Agulhas current is a warm current along Africa's east coast.
The warm Mozambique current flows between Madagascar and Africa into the Agulhas.
The West Australian current is cold.
The Somali current reverses direction with the monsoon.
The Indian Monsoon Drift flows clockwise in summer and anticlockwise in winter.
The Antarctic Circumpolar Current (West Wind Drift) encircles Antarctica.
The East Greenland current is cold; the Beaufort Gyre circulates clockwise in the western Arctic.
Tropical and subtropical west coasts bordered by cold currents are cool, foggy and arid.
Warm currents along tropical east coasts give warm, rainy climates.
Mixing of warm and cold currents gives fog and drizzle at Newfoundland.
Mixing zones of warm and cold currents are the best fishing grounds because plankton thrives there.
Hot deserts on west coasts (15°–30°) are trade-wind deserts aided by cold currents.
Warm water piled up by currents in the tropics fuels tropical cyclones.
Isohalines join places of equal salinity.
Salinity rises with evaporation and falls with precipitation, river inflow and melting ice.
The Red Sea (about 41‰) and Persian Gulf are the saltiest seas.
Lake Van (Turkey), the Dead Sea and the Great Salt Lake have extreme salinity.
The Baltic Sea and the Arctic Ocean are among the least saline waters.
The Bay of Bengal is less saline than the Arabian Sea because of Ganga–Brahmaputra inflow.
Ocean temperature has three layers: warm surface water, the thermocline (~500–1,000 m) and cold deep water.
Northern Hemisphere oceans are slightly warmer than southern ones.
The territorial sea extends 12 nautical miles and the contiguous zone 24.
The extended continental shelf may reach 350 nautical miles.
UNCLOS was adopted in 1982 and came into force in 1994.
The International Seabed Authority (Kingston, Jamaica) grants sea-bed exploration licences — not the Global Ocean Commission (UPSC 2021).
India holds an ISA licence for polymetallic nodules in the Central Indian Ocean Basin (~75,000 km²).
India was registered as a pioneer investor for sea-bed nodules in 1987.
Rare-earth minerals occur on the sea floor in international waters (UPSC 2021).
India also holds a licence for polymetallic sulphides on the Indian Ocean ridges.
Offshore oil and gas come from Mumbai High and the Krishna–Godavari basin (also gas hydrates).
OTEC needs a surface-to-deep temperature difference of about 20°C.
LTTD desalination plants at Kavaratti (Lakshadweep) use the ocean temperature difference.
Hornsea 2 (UK) is the largest operating offshore wind farm.
A 2024 re-measurement gives AP's coastline as about 1,053 km.
Placer minerals such as monazite and ilmenite occur on Kerala and AP beaches.
